claims.text: Argo CD syncs a commit whose image tag does not exist in the registry like any other: it compares manifests with live objects and does not check the registry; after the sync the Application is Synced.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Core Concepts (sync, sync status); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/gitops-revert.txt lines 1-2

claims.text: With the Deployment's default RollingUpdate strategy (no strategy set in api.yaml) and 2 replicas, the update creates one new Pod and removes no old Pod until a new one is ready (maxUnavailable 25% rounds down to 0, maxSurge 25% rounds up to 1).
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Deployments > Strategy > Rolling Update (Max Unavailable, Max Surge); envs/staging/api.yaml @ stage-3; output lines 3-4

claims.text: A Pod whose image tag does not exist reports waiting reason ErrImagePull (later ImagePullBackOff, the same failed pull); while it is not ready, the Application shows Progressing, not Healthy (a snapshot seconds after the sync).
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Images > ImagePullBackOff; Argo CD docs: Resource Health (Deployment); output lines 2-4

claims.text: kubectl rollout undo changes only the live Deployment (its Pod template back to the previous revision), not the manifest in Git; output prints 'deployment.apps/api rolled back' and the Deployment then names the previous tag.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Deployments > Rolling Back a Deployment; kubectl rollout undo; output lines 6-9

claims.text: With selfHeal on, after kubectl rollout undo the live Deployment differs from Git, Argo CD syncs again and the Deployment names the bad tag again shortly after (within the script's 120 s wait), with no new commit.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Self-Healing; gitops-revert.sh:38-41 and output lines 9-10 @ stage-3

claims.text: Without self-heal, a sync of any later commit applies every object of the Application and would set the api's tag back to the one Git names.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Sync Options > Selective Sync ('when syncing using auto sync Argo CD applies every object'); devops.l3.self-heal claim 5

claims.text: Argo CD can roll an Application back to a revision it synced earlier, but rollback cannot be performed against an Application with automated sync enabled.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy ('Rollback cannot be performed against an application with automated sync enabled'); argocd app rollback reference

claims.text: git revert creates a new commit whose change is the reverse of the given commit's; the reverted commit stays in the history. --no-edit uses the default message 'Revert "<subject>"' without opening an editor.
After the revert commit is pushed, Argo CD syncs it, the api rolls out on the previous tag, and the Application reports Synced, Healthy with 2 ready Pods on 1.0.0.
A revert changes only files in the config repository; migrations a hook already applied stay recorded in the database, so the older api runs against the newer schema.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Applying Migrations > Bundles (applies pending migrations, records them in the history table); devops.l3.ordering-a-sync

claims.text: Going back past a schema change works only when the older api was written to work with the newer schema; when it is not, the way forward is a new deploy commit naming an image that works with the newer schema.

git reset of main plus force-push (server branch made to match, commits may be dropped) makes Argo CD sync the good manifests; a clone that pulled the bad commit pushes a new one on top as a plain fast-forward (server branch is an ancestor), bringing it back.
claims.source_hint: git-scm.com/docs/git-reset, git-push (--force, fast-forward); Argo CD docs: Tracking and Deployment Strategies (targetRevision branch)

claims.text: When Argo CD manages a Deployment, a rollback should be a revert commit in the config repository rather than kubectl rollout undo or a reset and force-push.

claims.text: gitops-revert.sh: 38 rollout undo; 39 print tag right after; 40 wait up to 120 s for the bad tag; 48 git revert --no-edit HEAD; 50-51 push; 52-54 refresh, wait for sync, print Synced, Healthy; 55 rollout status; 56 api_images; 57 git log -n 3.
In the script, the bad commit and its revert each change only the api image line of envs/staging/api.yaml (the migration hook's tag is not changed); the captured run started from tag 1.0.0.
The elided output line after 'kubectl rollout undo' is a kubectl warning about Pod security settings; the capture hides commit ids in git log output as '...'.
